title: Pushup position guide lines
description:
Add two horizontal guide lines on the tracking screen to help users visualize valid pushup positions:

- **Lower line**: Shows the threshold where a movement counts as reaching the 'down' position (elbow ≤90°)
- **Upper line**: Shows the threshold where returning to 'up' position completes a full rep (elbow ≥160°)

Line specifications:
- Thin green lines spanning ~2/3 of screen width, horizontally centered
- Dynamic positioning based on detected shoulder height during the workout
- Lines flash/change color when the user crosses them
- Toggle button (matching FAB style) to show/hide the guide lines
- Visibility preference persisted via SharedPreferences

title: Track and display invalid rep reasons
description:
Add detailed tracking of why reps are marked invalid and provide user feedback.

**Requirements:**
1. Store invalid rep data for debugging:
   - Capture the reason (poor_form, partial_range, too_fast)
   - Store relevant angles/metrics at time of invalidation
   - Save to a debug log file or database table

2. Provide real-time user indication:
   - Show brief message explaining why rep was invalid
   - Options: text flash, badge, audio, skeleton highlight

**Current invalid reasons to track:**
- poor_form: Body deviation >30° for >40% of frames
- partial_range: Didn't reach full down/up position (to add)
- too_fast: Rep completed too quickly (existing debounce)

**Implementation notes:**
- Extend PushupCounter to return structured InvalidRepReason
- Create rep logging service for debug data
- Add UI component for displaying invalid reason feedback

title: Fix guide lines with calibration phase
description:
Redesign the guide lines feature to use a calibration-based approach instead of continuously tracking shoulder position.

**Current Problem**: Lines move dynamically following shoulders, which is confusing and doesn't provide stable guidance.

**New Approach**:
1. **Calibration Phase**: When workout starts, prompt user to do 1-2 calibration reps
2. **Learn Positions**: Record shoulder Y-positions during calibration up/down stages
3. **Lock Lines**: After calibration, lock lines in place as fixed targets
4. **Gradual Refinement**: Slowly adjust lines based on successful reps to dial in user's actual range
5. **Dual Display Mode**: Add setting to toggle between 'target positions' (goals to hit) vs 'threshold indicators' (showing what counts as valid)

This provides stable visual guidance while still adapting to the individual user's body and form.
close_reason: All tasks completed - calibration-based guide lines implemented

title: Implement gradual line refinement during workout
description:
After calibration, slowly refine line positions based on successful reps:
- On each valid rep, capture the actual up/down shoulder positions
- Apply very slow exponential moving average (e.g., 0.95/0.05 ratio)
- Only adjust if new position is within reasonable range of calibrated position
- Cap maximum drift from original calibration (e.g., ±10% of screen height)
- This helps dial in the user's actual comfortable range over time
close_reason: Added 5% refinement rate with 10% max drift cap

**Mode B - Threshold Indicators**:
- Lines show the detection thresholds (elbow 90°/160°)
- Labels: 'DOWN (90°)' and 'UP (160°)'
- Shows what the app is measuring

Store preference in SharedPreferences. This allows testing both approaches.

title: Simplify guide lines - remove calibration, keep single down line
description:
Simplify the guide lines feature based on user feedback:

**Remove:**
- Calibration phase (WorkoutState.calibrating)
- CalibrationOverlay widget
- Upper line (up position)
- Display mode toggle

**Keep:**
- Single lower line showing the 'down' position target
- Line positioned based on first pose detection, then locked
- FAB toggle to show/hide the line
- Flash feedback when crossing the line

**Implementation:**
1. Remove calibration state from WorkoutManager
2. Simplify GuideLinesOverlay to only track the down position
3. Set line position on first valid pose detection during workout
4. Lock the line position after initial detection
5. Remove CalibrationOverlay from tracking screen
6. Update GuideLinesPainter to only draw one line
close_reason: Simplified guide lines by removing calibration and keeping single down line that locks on first detection
